payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #349, slice 8 (the compiler walks raw JSON beside its typed tree): ask 8, "a `Dispatch` value type for the argv convention, with the engine executable resolved once and passed in".

Operator rulings:
- 2026-10-12: the structural splits (#288, #345 to #349) are mechanical, behaviour- and byte-preserving moves and typings with exact gates, scheduled by file contention, not difficulty.
- #349's earlier slices' rulings are on #349's comments (slices 1-7: #655, #669, #679, #681, #687, #709, #719); read them.
- 2026-09-26, the threat model: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.
- Decision 0063: Linux and macOS only. Decision 0009: `<engine> driver <kind> -- …`; the engine token is never matched on.
No compiled manifest, witness digest, refusal text or refusal order moves, and no BROKKR_BLESS is used.

THE BRANCH: story-349-slice-8 ends at 5a684b65. The story (implement-story-349-the-compiler-07f10c74; review residual LOW, no security residual) built 551efa6a on main b6475fda. The controller then STACKED it on #288's slices L and M (story-288-slice-m, abf62629, on main d13ce473, landing as one PR in parallel), and re-signed it as 5a684b65. Why stacked: this slice lowers quality/suppressions.txt's production too_many_arguments count (23 -> 22), on the line beside the too_many_lines count that #288's slices K, L and M lower. Git merges edits on adjacent lines as a conflict, so landed beside each other, the second would need a rebase and a new vouch. Stacked, this slice's patch is unchanged when L and M merge. The one rebase conflict was those two lines, resolved to `22 too_many_arguments` and `21 too_many_lines`. JUDGE THIS SLICE'S OWN COMMIT, 5a684b65, against its parent abf62629.

What 5a684b65 does (33 files):
- brokkr-runtime's new module argv.rs (82 lines; tests in argv/tests.rs) holds `Dispatch`, which reads an argv as decision 0009's convention: `[_, "driver", kind, rest..]` with exactly one leading `--` stripped, else `Raw`. The seven hand matches read it: bundle.rs built_in_model_driver (its kind list applied to the parsed kind) and dispatch_driver; engine.rs is_exec_dispatch, which engine/boxed.rs now calls instead of its copy; agents.rs permission_template and inline_template (the refused arm unchanged); capabilities.rs harness_of.
- argv.rs also holds `Executable`, resolved once by `Executable::current()` at Bundle::compile_with_capabilities (which compile, compile_with, compile_under, compile_unmapped and compile_with_realm funnel into) and at brokkr-cli's muninn.rs:517. The bundle carries it (`Bundle::executable`); the engine reads it for hands_command, the Harness arm, isolation's Transport and the dialect step. In brokkr-runtime production, `current_exe` is read only in Executable::current and in engine/broker/observation.rs:30 (decision 0065 slice two's file, left as a follow-up). Unreadable spellings are kept: brokkr_executable(None) -> "brokkr"; `or_empty` -> "" where unwrap_or_default() stood.
- bundle/expand.rs (73 lines) takes the `{brokkr}` expansion; bundle.rs 5232 -> 5145 on the stack (row 5185 after slice K). engine.rs stays at its 3523 row, agents.rs 1553 (row 1554 after slice M), capabilities.rs at its 1939 row.
- Public API (quality/public-api/brokkr-runtime.txt), four changes, each with a cross-crate consumer:
  (i) `expand_command` takes `&Executable` first (muninn.rs);
  (ii) compose_site and compose_site_at's boxed tuple is now (&Executable, &Path, Option<&Sealed>) (driver_conformance.rs, capability_launch.rs);
  (iii) the pub field `Bundle::executable` (brokkr-cli recipes/tests.rs's Bundle literal);
  (iv) the new pub module `brokkr_runtime::argv` with `pub struct Executable` and `pub fn current()`.
- The compile's new carriage is anonymous tuples ((boundary, engine) into SiteCompiler::new and CapabilityWalk::of; (engine, dir) into parse_command and the record_* functions; assemble's (library_root, adapters_root) and (realm_name, dialect, law)), the last retiring assemble's too_many_arguments expect.
- Tests: every_reader_of_the_dispatch_convention_answers_from_one_reading (the table over the seven sites); the injection tests a_compile_expands_brokkr_to_the_executable_it_is_handed, a_box_and_its_hands_server_name_the_executable_they_are_handed, a_harness_fragment_names_the_executable_it_is_handed, a_dialect_step_dispatches_through_the_executable_its_bundle_carries, the_whole_set_is_run_by_the_executable_the_bundle_carries (engine/boundary_tests/sealed_tests/executable_tests.rs, 166 lines); removal controls recorded in the commit message. witness_digests:: 6/6 with no BROKKR_BLESS; all 19 recipes compile byte-identically on base and head (the implementer's artifact).
- Host exact coverage on 551efa6a (the story's head, on b6475fda) was 100%. On the stacked 5a684b65 it is 100% (63902/63902 lines, 8254/8254 branches, 8176/8176 functions), and host lints, the crap ratchet on fresh LCOV and the API ratchet hold. Clippy (workspace, all targets, -D warnings), suppressions:: (6) and witness_digests:: (6) pass on 5a684b65 (controller).
- The story review's surviving findings, carried:
  - F1 LOW (decision 0071 ruling 9; the story text "An unreadable executable keeps today's exact behaviour at each site ... Bind each with a test"): two of the five engine sites bind only the injected path. isolation::beside's Transport and the dialect step have no Executable(None) row, while compile, hands_command and the Harness arm each do. A re-read of current_exe at either site is caught; a site-level change of the unreadable spelling is not (the accessors are unit-pinned). Fix: one None row at each of the two sites.
  - F2 INFO: the public API grew beyond the story's named expand_command change; the PR's Ruling: line names all four above.
  - F3 INFO (ruling 10): anonymous tuples rather than a named parameter object; the house's boxed/worktree tuples set the precedent.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on the HEAD binary and tests (this slice's diff is abf62629..5a684b65):
1. Behaviour and bytes: for each of the seven readers, compare its body at abf62629 with HEAD's, and confirm every argv class answers as before (len 0, 1, 2, no marker, no escape, one escape, two escapes, exec and each kind). witness_digests:: with no BROKKR_BLESS; every recipe in recipes/ compiles byte-identically on an abf62629 build and HEAD (separate target dir; build it yourself).
2. The executable: resolved once per process entry that compiles; no brokkr-runtime production read of current_exe outside Executable::current and observation.rs:30; each of the five engine sites and the compile names exactly the injected path (reproduce one injection yourself). On F1, say whether the story's "Bind each with a test" requires the two missing None rows, and if so RETURN it as a finding for the implement phase (add the Executable(None) row at isolation::beside's Transport and at the dialect step, each asserting today's exact spelling, with a compiling removal control).
3. The stack: `git range-diff b6475fda..551efa6a abf62629..5a684b65` shows only the suppressions resolution; the counts (22 too_many_arguments, 21 too_many_lines) equal the suppressions test's.
4. Standards: CC 15 or under and 100 lines or under for every new or changed function (cargo crap); quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; no file over its row (bundle.rs, engine.rs, agents.rs, capabilities.rs).
5. Scope and contention: no engine/broker/** or bundle/compose.rs hunk; agents.rs hunks only in permission_template and inline_template; engine.rs hunks only the import, the carrying tuples, is_exec_dispatch, compose_site/compose_site_at/Composing and the Harness arm. Nothing under contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/.
6. For the PR: name every ruling needed. Expected: the four public API changes (i)-(iv); the anonymous-tuple carriage; F1 (closed here if returned, else accepted as a follow-up). Name the follow-ups: brokkr-protocol native_controls.rs's two hand matches on the convention; current_exe in engine/broker/observation.rs (U8a2b), brokkr-protocol hands.rs, adapters.rs and adapters/mcp.rs, brokkr-cli broker/session.rs and verbs/probe.rs; ask 5's second half (roles as compiled Bundle fields), which needs a decision first.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked (timeout 590); cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test capability_launch --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- recipes:: init_stacks:: suppressions:: machine_proof:: muninn:: driver_conformance:: portable_recipes:: witness; typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; `cargo crap --path crates/brokkr-runtime/src --format json` for every function you add or change; git diff --check.

Other work runs in parallel. Decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat) runs U8a2b on brokkr-runtime engine/broker* and engine.rs at the admission, exclusion and dispatch-door/claim sites; settled with it on 2026-10-18: whoever lands second rebases. #288 slices L and M are this branch's parents, landing as their own PR. #744, #735 and #753 touch none of this slice's files.

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" if a fix is needed, and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",

    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest.   ],
```
